Prepared only. Publication and dispatch wait for the qualified b5933c08 readiness/lifecycle harness and independent peer review. The runtime is unchanged BASE 1f33. The separately bound harness source includes Node's corrected timer boundary. Historical Node timings are not comparable. This pilot produces no candidate samples or statistical claim.

One hosted AMD64 pilot covers all 70 remaining category leaves: HTTPD 42, Node 4, Ruby 4 and Redis 20. Native runc controls run first for all four categories. Full BASE systrap execution follows, partitioning HTTPD by named concurrency. The first HTTPD group must prove the actual Go selector's exact nine-leaf set before larger payloads; the final union must contain all 42 leaves. HTTPD uses N=concurrency: 10,434 requests and 15,005,577,216 bytes (~13.98GiB) of known static 200-response payload, excluding 404 bodies and headers. Its one-wave workload does not establish statistical adequacy.

Node and Ruby use N=1000, or 4000 requests each. Source values bound Node at 0..4 KiB plus template per response and Ruby at 5 KiB plus template. Native small controls add~10MiB HTTPD payload and~4/5MiB Node/Ruby values. Redis uses 1000 requests for each of 20 leaves, plus tool-owned setup and five spaced readiness pings per parent benchmark. This does not imply a fixed total wire byte count. Native preflight captures redis-benchmark version, help, default value size and client count, plus actual HTTPD file lengths. Metadata commands accept exit 0/1 only with specific positive output; timeout or unsupported output fails. There is no source image build fallback or broad image pull.

Canonical Make/Bazel builds BASE's complete opaque release once and preserves its tar, hash and full fileset manifest. One repaired canonical harness set is built with all runfiles materialized. Bazel shuts down before execution. The complete release is installed at one active path. Docker configuration is preserved and restored; bounded restart and actual exact-path readiness precede controls. Each visit verifies every runtime/harness member, immutable image IDs, runtime configuration and quiescence before and after execution.

Accounting requires exact leaves and N, finite nonnegative metrics and positive rates. Canonical CLI latency rounding may legitimately produce zero; rates must remain positive. Skips, failures, missing metrics, nonfinite values and orphan containers fail the pilot. Raw Go output, argv, observed duration and dependency metadata are retained. Hosted noise and one visit do not establish variability or statistical qualification. The pilot's actual durations replace speculative campaign costs.

Outer 177 min plus 180 s cleanup grace is ≤180 min. Phase caps are: specific image pulls 30 min; dependency metadata 2 min; BASE release 20 min; archive/freeze 2 min; combined harness build 25 min; cquery 2 min; harness freeze/manifest 3 min; shutdown 2 min; runtime activation~3.4min; native controls 14 min; four categories 60 min; accounting 2 min. Total~165.4min plus small shell overhead, bounded by the 177 min global deadline. Cleanup budgets total 152 s, inclusive of kill grace, and restore SOURCE first.

Native cases have 180 s caps. HTTPD groups have 170 s caps inside the 15 min category deadline. Other categories have 840 s caps inside their 15 min deadline. An exceeded cap produces a failed capability receipt; variants are never omitted or called partial qualification.

Canonical Go calibration runs each leaf once at N=1 before the requested fixed count when N>1. This adds 33 HTTPD requests and 50,075,648 known static response bytes: expected total 10,467 requests and 15,055,652,864 static body bytes, excluding readiness requests, 404 bodies and headers. Node/Ruby each execute 4004 requests and Redis 20,020 requested operation executions, plus Redis tool setup/readiness. Printed sample N remains the requested fixed count and validators still require that exact value. Native controls also include their initial calibration request. These counts describe application requests, not physical wire traffic.

Redis's canonical source retries infinity output up to three times per invocation. Thus 20,020 requested operations is the one-attempt workload, not an observed exact total; the known retry bound is 60,060, plus tool setup/readiness. Native Redis's one-leaf control similarly requests 1,001 to 3,003 operations before setup. This pilot records actual walltime and final metrics but does not invent an unlogged retry count or wire-byte total.
